newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch builders see three percent growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch builders see three percent growth in 1997.

text.p: The volume of Dutch building production is set to grow by three percent in 1997, a survey by Dutch construction industry body EIB showed on Wednesday.
All sectors are seen contributing to the increase, with residential construction and civil engineering growing by three percent and non-residential construction rising by 4.5 percent.
The volume of maintenance and renovation work is seen rising by some two percent, EIB said.
In the period 1997-2002, building production is seen increasing by some one percent annually, it added.
EIB said that the previously expected slowdown in Dutch housing construction was unlikely to materialise.
While demographic trends pointed towards a falling demand for new housing, this had been amply compensated by the growing demand for higher-quality accommodation, it said.
"Given the favourable market conditions, such as low mortgage rates and a real rise in family incomes, residential construction is unlikely to falter in the near term," it said.
